analysis:
Examined the changed files: the CI path classifier (scripts/ci-component-paths.py head line 16 adds .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml to COMMON), the docs-impact rule (scripts/docs-impact-rules.json line 78), the routing test (scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py hunk at ~241-244 now expects a `route` job and lanes with `needs: [changes, route]`), and the docs/operations/provider-release.md excerpt (units 2f70cfa5bbfcf760:5 shows the release publication flow; the patch notes that only pull-request runs can use Darkbloom Sandboxes while master and dispatched runs always use Blacksmith runners).

Security-relevant behavior: a change to the new route workflow now selects all components, which is fail-safe (more CI, not less). No change to the provider runtime, WebSocket contract (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), release signing, or registration. The documented release flow is unchanged: signing has no R2 credentials, staging is separate, and registration remains hash-pinned, with official registration not granting serving permission.

Remaining unverified contract: the darkbloom-route.yml workflow itself and the updated ci.yml are not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the `route` job holds no secrets, that untrusted fork PRs cannot select self-hosted Darkbloom Sandbox runners with elevated privileges, or that the runner routing keeps release and signing jobs on Blacksmith. That is the key integration question for a later pass, since PR code executing on a new runner class is CI supply-chain surface (ADV-003). The release signing jobs, per the docs, run only on master or dispatch, which the docs say use Blacksmith. No finding is raised because no changed lines show a concrete weakness.
